title: The MAC Address Table: The Complete Beginner's Guide

scenes.narration: How does a switch know which cable leads to which computer? Nobody tells it. It simply watches and takes notes.

scenes.heading: The hotel guest directory
scenes.narration: You're the front desk clerk at a big hotel. Every time a guest sends something, you note their name and room number. That's the switch learning the source M A C address. When a delivery arrives for a known guest, you send it straight to the room. For an unknown guest, you page every room, which is called flooding. Entries expire after five minutes without activity.

scenes.heading: Three decisions
scenes.narration: For every frame, the switch makes one of three decisions. Forward: the guest is in a different room, so send it there. Filter: the guest is on the same port, so drop it. Flood: nobody knows this guest, so send it everywhere else.

scenes.heading: Common mix-ups
scenes.narration: Three mix-ups. A switch learns from the source address, not the destination. It doesn't flood everything just because the table is empty. And static entries never age out.
